why: I checked each verifier check against the words of its expect line. Checks 1, 2 and 4 hold. Check 1 tests only that clamp is exported and that its results stay limited to lo..hi, including edge cases those words cover. Check 2 tests only that lo>hi throws a RangeError. Check 4 tests only that `npm test` exits 0. Check 3 breaks the rule. Its FAIL condition rests on the regex `'\\b'+n+'\\s*\\('`, which fails any exported function whose name is not followed by an opening parenthesis somewhere in README.md. The line "README.md documents every function math.js exports" does not require that form. A README could document `clamp` fully under a heading like "clamp" or "`clamp` — returns…" and still fail with "MISSING". That is a wording/format rule inside a FAIL condition when it belongs under Advisory. The output does have an Advisory section, but this stricter test is not in it.
